note: Shared verdicts of css-support.json for the exporter's lint and the Unity compiler.

Each case puts one declaration (`property: value`, sometimes with a helper declaration after `;`) on the element with data-u-id="case" of a context page, a 2560×1440 screen with the kit font and a border-box reset; `{decl}` in the context css marks where it goes.

`lint` lists the error rule ids the lint must report (empty: the design passes), `notes` the warning and info rule ids; both are written by hand and checked by tools/design-export/test/css-support-cases.test.ts.

`export` is ok when the exporter builds the IR, `ir` is that IR (null when export fails) and `unity` what the Unity compiler must do with it: compile, reject (the IR carries the rejected declaration), or null (no IR, or the exporter drops or rewrites the value so lint is the only gate). `export`, `ir` and `unity` are regenerated with UPDATE_CONTRACTS=1 and otherwise must not change.
`lintOnlyRules` are judged from the rendered page (boxes, runtime pseudo-states) and cannot be seen in the IR: a case rejected only by them must still compile in Unity.
`kitRules` are judged against the project's kit: the Unity side agrees only when it compiles with the kit's font map and text-styles.json.

Unity: a C# test reads this file, compiles every case's `ir` (IrReader, Lowering, StyleMapper / ScreenBuilder) and must agree with `unity`; when the mapper reports a rule id (css-support.json error properties, rejectedValues, valueRule), it should equal one of `lint`.
